PyTorch explicitly warns that mathematically equivalent batched and singleton computations need not be bitwise identical; a packed-versus-singleton tolerance failure alone cannot establish a padding defect. For PyTorch 2.5.1, disable both `torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32` and `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32`, disable autocast, and use evaluation mode. These controls reduce precision-related differences without guaranteeing identical execution. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html), [2.5.1 CUDA guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.5.1/docs/source/notes/cuda.rst).

Construct an independent FP64 recurrence by promoting identical weights, inputs and initial states before arithmetic. Respect gate order `(r,z,n)` and PyTorch’s equations: `r=σ(xWrᵀ+bir+hUrᵀ+bhr)`, similarly for `z`; `n=tanh(xWnᵀ+bin+r⊙(hUnᵀ+bhn))`; `h′=(1−z)⊙n+z⊙h`. The reset gate multiplies the recurrent affine result, including its bias. Compare packed and unpadded singleton outputs separately against this reference. For left-padded histories, first compact real tokens into valid prefixes for packing; verify lengths, restored batch order and final nonpadding readout. This diagnostic procedure distinguishes indexing errors from numerical discrepancies; FP64 remains a reference, not exact arithmetic. [Version-pinned GRU implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.5.1/torch/nn/modules/rnn.py).

Report score errors, top-10 set differences and within-set ordering differences separately. Ordering changes alone cannot change HR@10. Inspect the tenth/eleventh score margin: if every score perturbation is bounded by ε, a boundary gap greater than 2ε guarantees unchanged membership. Near ties can change membership despite small numerical errors; investigate against the reference rather than declaring a padding defect from an arbitrary tolerance.
